about: The user wants orbit to commit its work to the program's pull request the whole time a program runs, with the pull request opened at the program's first architect session and merged by the user at the end. R-adf-1 says every setting defaults to today's behaviour. Today orbit commits only in a project that turns pull requests on, and then when a change is proposed, when it is archived, and when work is handed to another reviewer; a project that sets nothing gets no commits from orbit.
question: Should committing throughout the program be a setting that is off by default (R-adf-1 unchanged), or what orbit does by default (amending R-adf-1 and G0)?

defines.definition: the one git branch a program's changes land on when the project sets pr: per-architecture; the program pull request merges it into the main branch
